donorReadme: - `io-2k.jpg` / `io-4k.jpg`
- Source: USGS Astrogeology Io Galileo SSI Global Color Merge Mosaic 1km, combining Galileo/Voyager terrain imagery with Galileo colour
- Source page: https://astrogeology.usgs.gov/search/map/io_galileo_ssi_global_color_merge_mosaic_1km
- Download endpoint used: `https://planetarymaps.usgs.gov/mosaic/Io_Galileo_SSI_Global_Mosaic_ClrMerge_1km.tif`
- Credit: USGS Astrogeology Science Center; NASA/JPL Galileo and Voyager missions
- License: public domain; source lists no use constraints
- Purpose: improve terrain detail using the colour-merged product rather than the previous `FalseColor` derivative
- Processing: converted the `11445x5723` RGB TIFF with Lanczos resizing to `2048x1024` (quality 90) and `4096x2048` (quality 92) optimized progressive JPEGs; no synthetic detail or Juno patches
- Selection: 2K below 768px viewport width; 4K at 768px and above

- Projection: simple cylindrical, planetocentric latitude, positive-west longitudes from -180 to 180; raster runs from 180 W through 0 W to 180 W, equivalent to east-positive -180 to +180 left to right; north at top
- Alignment: retained source orientation and existing east-positive feature coordinates; Loki, Pele, and Prometheus checked visually on the globe
- Limitations: mixed native resolution, visible mosaic boundaries, interpolated polar coverage, and enhanced colours; this is a historical composite, not a current Juno global map

coordinates.placement: latLonToXYZ in the donor src/entities/hotspot.ts, on Three.js SphereGeometry UVs
coordinates.longitudeDegrees: exactly as stored in features.json, placed by latLonToXYZ whatever the range; the donor stores values already in its own marker frame (see longitudeRange, markerLongitudeFromSource and donorReadmeNote)
coordinates.position: [radius * sin(phi) * sin(theta), radius * cos(phi), radius * sin(phi) * cos(theta)]
coordinates.conventionNote: donor: raster is equivalent to east-positive -180 to +180 left to right; existing east-positive feature coordinates retained
coordinates.donorReadmeNote: - The current Io release uses the USGS/NASA global mosaic at `2K`; the source includes original mission mosaic boundaries and polar coverage gaps, but it is correctly shaped for sphere texturing and avoids the stretched/non-standard dimensions of the previous local asset.
